title: Inactivation of Pathogens via Visible-Light Photolysis of Riboflavin-5′-Phosphate
protocol: Mount six LED lights (DC 12 V) on the inside of an opaque plastic cup (8 cm x 7 cm).
Add reactants into glass test tubes (13 mm in diameter and 100 mm in height).
Secure the test tubes at the top of the cup.
Place the experimental setup in a room with a steady temperature of 25 ± 3 °C.
Monitor and record the temperature of test units throughout the photolytic reactions by an infrared thermometer.
Prepare a 0.1 mM FMN solution in 100 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.8).
Expose FMN samples (3 mL each) to blue, green, red, or violet light at an intensity of 10 W/m2 for 5 min.
Keep 3 mL of FMN solution in the dark as a control.
Record the absorbance of irradiated FMN samples in the 250-750 nm range using a UV/Visible spectrophotometer.
Add 109.3 mg of L-methionine to 73.3 mL of PB (100 mM; pH 7.8).
Vortex the solution to dissolve the L-methionine.
After the L-methionine is fully dissolved, add 10 mg of NBT powder and 1.53 mL of 0.117 mM FMN to the solution.
Expose the reaction solution (1 mL) to blue or violet LED light irradiation at 10 W/m2 for 1-5 min.
Transmit a colony of S. aureus(BCRC 10451) from a cultured plate into 10 mL of Lysogeny broth in a 15 mL screw-capped test tube.
Culture the S. aureus at 37 °C for 16 h in a shaker.
Transfer 0.5 mL of the culture to a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube and dilute with sterilized water to an optical density of 0.5 at 600 nm (~6 x 10^7 CFU/mL).
Centrifuge the diluted culture at 14,000 x g for 10 min and decant the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of FMN-buffered solution (30, 60, and 120 µM FMN in PB) to the cell pellets and vortex.
For irradiated control, add 1 mL of PB alone to a sample.
Transfer 1 mL each of viable bacterial cell solutions containing 30 µM FMN and PB alone into glass tubes and irradiate them with violet light at 10 W/m2 for 30 min.
Transfer 1 mL each of viable bacterial cell solutions containing 30, 60, and 120 µM FMN and PB alone into glass tubes and irradiate them with blue light at 20 W/m2 for 120 min.
Set up another glass tube with 1 mL of viable bacterial cell solution containing 120 µM FMN and irradiate it with blue light at 20 W/m2 for 60 min.
Set up test tubes as dark controls and cover them with thick aluminum foils.
Keep the irradiation chamber and dark controls in a cold room at 9 ± 1 °C during the 30-120 min irradiation period.
Transfer 0.2 mL from each of the reaction solutions onto a Luria agar (LA) plate after irradiation.
Spread the bacteria over the LA plate using an L-shaped glass rod.
Incubate the plates overnight at 37 °C.
Calculate the viable plate count and inactivation rates of S. aureus after overnight growth.
Define the inactivation rate of S. aureus as [1 - I / D] × 100%, where I is the number of CFUs in the irradiated sample, and D is the number of CFUs in the dark control.
Dilute bacterial density samples with sterilized water to an optical density of 0.5 at 600 nm (~6 x 10^6 CFU/mL).
Transfer 0.5 mL of the culture to a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the mixture at 14,000 x g for 10 min and decant the supernatant.
Add 0.1093 g of L-methionine, 0.1 g of NBT, and 25 mL of FMN (400, 240, or 120 µM) to 75 mL of PB.
For each 1 mL of the reactant applied, adjust the final concentrations of FMN, methionine, and NBT as specified.
Add 1 mL of each reactant solution to the cell pellets.
Irradiate the solutions by violet light at 10 W/m2 for 10 min.
Centrifuge the mixture at 14,000 x g for 10 min and decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to extract reduced NBT.
Detect the produced species from the absorbance at 560 nm.
